correctness.rationale: For every occupied part the defining closed-neighborhood inequality is exactly \(s-s_i\ge t=\lfloor (r-1)n/2\rfloor\). One-vertex deletion analysis proves at least two capped parts iff local minimality; the separate two-tight-parts argument proves no nonempty proper defensive suballiance can survive. For maximality, t-n falls in [0,(r-2)n], yielding the full-part construction. Inclusion-exclusion weights equal one when at least two parts attain cap and zero otherwise. Literal adjacency verifier confirms 145,206 nonempty subsets across 10 small graphs and 10 further weighted profiles; these finite checks supplement a proof valid for all \(r\ge3,n\ge2\).

value.rationale: The upper defensive alliance number is a named maximum-size minimality invariant whose computation is hard on unrestricted graphs. A sharp exact formula, a proof that local and global minimality coincide for this natural highly symmetric family, and the entire cardinality distribution—including the number of maximum configurations—form a motivated complete classification of a nontrivial infinite two-parameter graph class. The content goes beyond a minimum parameter or a trivial consequence of raw all-alliance polynomial coefficients; globally minimality must be analyzed separately. The formula is elementary but nontrivial and independently interpretable.
